dixMais.setupDesc: A perfect person, a solid 10 out of 10, with one flaw. You each give your new rating, then compare.
dixMais.modeTitre: How do you want to play?
dixMais.relaisNote: Pass the phone: no peeking at the rating.
dixMais.deuxDix: Still a 10 for both of you!
dixMais.deuxRedhib: A dealbreaker for both of you.
dixMais.ecartMoyen: Not quite on the same page... Want to talk about it?
dixMais.resSur: Out of the {{total}} cards you played
dixMais.accordLegende: of cards rated within one point
dixMais.res_haut_t: You judge things the same way
dixMais.res_haut_d: On most cards, your ratings were within a point of each other. What bugs one of you bugs the other, and what makes one of you laugh makes the other laugh too. You'll still argue like everyone else, but you draw the line in the same place.
dixMais.res_milieu_t: On the same page for the big stuff
dixMais.res_milieu_d: You agree a lot of the time, just not always. The cards where your ratings split are actually the most interesting ones: that's where you find out what the other person can't stand, or what they let slide without a second thought.
dixMais.res_bas_d: Your ratings rarely line up. That's totally fine, it just means you don't draw the line in the same place. Have a look at your biggest disagreements below, that's where the conversation gets fun!
dixMais.memeExigence: You're about as strict as each other.
dixMais.plusSevere: {{nom}} is the tougher judge: {{a}} on average, versus {{b}} for {{autre}}.
dixMais.blocRedhib: A dealbreaker for both of you
